primary_task: Add an iOS App Clip target to an Expo app and ship it: configure app.json and targets/clip, register bundle IDs with Apple, host the AASA file via EAS Hosting, and build and submit to TestFlight.

requirements.name: bun / bunx (with @bacons/apple-targets)
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, apt from Ubuntu, go modules, nuget, GitHub release downloads) ..." (bun is on npm and in GitHub releases)

requirements.name: Apple Developer Program account
requirements.evidence: "Shipping one requires an Apple Developer Program membership and App Store review" ; step 4 `bunx setup-safari`: "This logs in to the Apple Developer account, registers `com.bacon.may20`, creates the App Store Connect entry"
requirements.basis: lacks: "accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers such as AWS, Azure and GCP, SaaS products, model hubs, app stores, email delivery, payment)"

requirements.name: Apple developer / App Store Connect hosts
requirements.evidence: step 4 `bunx setup-safari` registers bundle IDs and creates the App Store Connect entry; step 9 `bunx testflight` uploads
requirements.basis: "Network egress goes through an allow-list proxy: the package registries and hosts pypi (PyPI), npm, GitHub (github.com, api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com), Ubuntu (apt archives), NuGet and the Go module proxy are open; other hosts are refused (for example huggingface, Microsoft Learn and Azure, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA)."

requirements.name: EAS (expo.dev) account and hosting: eas deploy, EAS Build, eas metadata
requirements.evidence: step 7 "The AASA file must be live before iOS will trust the association. Use EAS Hosting: ... eas deploy --prod" ; step 9 `bunx testflight` ("uses your EAS plan's build minutes") ; step 10 `eas metadata:push`
requirements.basis: egress_deny: "expo.dev", "*.expo.dev"; lacks: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: ... other hosts are refused, for example huggingface.co, Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA"

requirements.name: publishes / writes_external (deploy website, TestFlight submission, App Store metadata push)
requirements.evidence: "eas deploy --prod" ; "Build, upload, and schedule a TestFlight submission." ; "eas metadata:push"

requirements.name: expo CLI (npx expo / bunx expo)
requirements.evidence: "bunx expo config" ; "bunx expo customize src/app/+html.tsx" ; "bunx expo export -p web" ; "npx expo config --type introspect"
requirements.basis: "bash": "... install packages from the open registries (... npm ...)"

requirements.name: curl
requirements.basis: "bash": "run shell commands on Linux x86_64 ..." (standard Linux software; the target host *.expo.app is not on the allow-list)

blocking: egress:Apple developer / App Store Connect hosts
platform:EAS (expo.dev) account and hosting: eas deploy, EAS Build, eas metadata
other:publishes / writes_external (deploy website, TestFlight submission, App Store metadata push)
notes: I took the numbered steps 1-10 as the required workflow (the doc's "What you get" lists the hosted AASA and a TestFlight build). Under the other reading, where the primary task is only 'add the App Clip target' (steps 1-3 and 6, 8: editing app.json, `bun create target clip`, targets/clip config, +html.tsx), everything needed is installable from npm and the verdict would be ACHIEVABLE. The App Clip build itself also implies Xcode/macOS, but the document routes it through EAS cloud builds, so I did not list Xcode separately. The submit-expo-feedback command is optional.
